'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations]]
****[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] says that [[Israel]] has agreed to stop the [[airstrike]]s on [[Iran]] at [[United States]] [[President of the United States|president]] [[Donald Trump]]'s request, but an official states that Israeli attacks on [[southern Lebanon]] will continue. Netanyahu also warns that Israel will respond if Iran resumes [[Islamic Republic of Iran Armed Forces|military]] action. [https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/2006160 (AFP via ''Dawn'')] [https://aje.news/5n8ezy?update=4636916 (Al Jazeera)]
***[[2026 Iranian strikes on Israel]]
****The [[Israeli Air Force]] launches strikes against military sites in [[Western Iran|western]] and [[Central Iran|central]] [[Iran]], making it the first time Israel launched strikes against Iran since the [[2026 Iran war ceasefire|April 7]] [[ceasefire]]. The strikes come as Iranian state media reported explosions were heard in [[Isfahan]], [[Kermanshah]], [[Tabriz]], and [[Tehran]]. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-898666 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/428279 (Israel National News)]
****The [[Islamic Republic of Iran Armed Forces|Iranian military]] says that attacks on Israel will resume if it continues the [[2026 Lebanon war|war against Lebanon]]. [https://aje.news/5n8ezy?update=4636716 (Al Jazeera)]
***[[2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region]]
****The [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] launches strikes in the [[Sulaymaniyah Governorate]] against the [[Kurdistan Freedom Party|Kurdish opposition group]] headquarters in the [[Kurdistan region]] of [[Iraq]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-strikes-headquarters-of-kurdish-opposition-groups-in-northern-iraq-amid-tensions-with-israel/3959671 (AA)]
***[[2026 Houthi strikes on Israel]]
****The [[Houthi]]s fire two missiles at Israel, one of which was intercepted, and another that did not reach it. [https://aje.news/5n8ezy?update=4636545 (Al Jazeera)] 
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[List of current ambassadors from Iran|Iran ambassador]] to [[Russia]] [[Kazem Jalali]] tells the [[List of newspapers in Russia|Russian newspaper]] ''[[Izvestia]]'' that the [[Strait of Hormuz]] will reopen, but with new conditions set by [[Iran]] and [[Oman]], including transit fees. [https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/hormuz-strait-will-be-open-with-transit-fees-iran-envoy-moscow-quoted-2026-06-08/ (Reuters)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Israel Defense Forces]] confirms that they have killed three [[Palestinian Islamic Jihad]] militants in the central [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-898747 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Kashmir conflict]], [[List of protests in Pakistan|Protests in Pakistan]]
**Eleven people, including four [[Azad Kashmir Police|police]] officers, are killed and dozens others are injured during clashes between police and supporters of the [[List of organisations banned in Pakistan|banned]] [[Joint Awami Action Committee]] (JAAC) in [[Azad Kashmir]], [[Pakistan]]. Police arrest more than 70 JAAC members. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/8/at-least-11-killed-in-pakistan-administered-kashmir-clashes-before-rally (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**A U.S.-led coalition consisting of [[Belgium]], [[France]], [[Germany]], [[Greece]], [[Italy]], [[Norway]], and the [[United Kingdom]] endorses a civilian-led political dialogue for [[Sudan]] to end the war under the facilitation of the [[African Union]], the [[Arab League]], the [[European Union]], [[Intergovernmental Authority on Development|IGAD]], and the [[United Nations]]. [https://www.capitalfm.co.ke/news/2026/06/us-led-coalition-sudan-civilian-dialogue-au-igad-eu-un/ (Capital FM Kenya)] [https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/western-powers-regional-blocs-back-civilian-led-roadmap-for-sudan (Radio Tamazuj)]

'''Business and economy'''

**The [[Iraqi Civil Aviation Authority]] reopens [[Iraq]]'s airspace after [[Iran]] announced that it was halting attacks against [[Israel]]. Additionally, [[Syria]] reopens its airspace, including resuming operations at the [[Damascus International Airport]]. *[[Foreign relations of Kyrgyzstan]], [[Foreign relations of the European Union]]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Mindanao earthquake]]
**A {{M|w|7.8}} earthquake, whose epicenter is located off [[Maasim, Sarangani|Maasim]], [[Sarangani]], [[Philippines]], strikes [[Mindanao]], hitting as far as [[Leyte]], the provinces of [[North Maluku]] and [[North Sulawesi]], [[Indonesia]], and [[Sabah]], [[Malaysia]]. At least 35 people are killed while more than 200 others are injured and 12 are missing. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2242307/magnitude-7-8-quake-rocks-mindanao-topples-buildings-disrupts-classes (AFP and AP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jun/08/philippines-earthquake-mindanao-tsunami-warnings (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2026/06/08/tsunami-advisory-issued-for-sabahs-east-coast-after-powerful-mindanao-quake-rattles-region/222903 (''Malay Mail'')] [https://www.philstar.com/nation/2026/06/08/2533701/general-santos-mindanao-quake-upgraded-magnitude-78 (''The Philippine Star'')]
** [[Tsunami]]s are recorded in [[Guam]], [[Palau]] and parts of Indonesia, [[Japan]], and the Philippines. The [[Pacific Tsunami Warning Center]] (PTWC) cancels its tsunami advisory issued for Guam and the [[Northern Mariana Islands]]; while agencies in [[Australia]], Malaysia, and [[New Zealand]] lift their respective warnings. The PTWC later confirms that the tsunami threat passes hours following its issuance of the warning for parts of the [[Pacific Islands|Pacific]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/c20y4xp43ywt (BBC News)] [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20260608_690/ (NHK)] [https://www.straitstimes.com/live-earthquake-hits-southern-philippines-june8 (''The Straits Times'')] [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/pacific/597554/tsunami-advisories-issued-for-parts-of-pacific-after-7-point-8-earthquake-in-philippines (RNZ)] [https://www.tsunami.gov/events/PHEB/2026/06/07/26158002/6/WEPA40/WEPA40.txt (tsunami.gov)]
**[[President of the Philippines|Philippine president]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] orders the suspension of classes in affected areas across Mindanao, coinciding with the country's first day of the new school year. [https://asia.nikkei.com/economy/natural-disasters/one-dead-damage-reported-after-7.8-magnitude-quake-hits-south-philippines (''Nikkei Asia'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Armenian parliamentary election]]
**Preliminary results from yesterday's election reveal that the governing [[Civil Contract (Armenia)|Civil Contract]] party won 49.8% of votes, translating to a [[parliamentary majority]], but falling short of the two-thirds majority required to call a [[constitutional referendum]] for a peace deal with [[Azerbaijan]] and the restart of border trade with [[Turkey]]. Opposition alliances [[Strong Armenia]] and [[Armenia Alliance]] entered parliament after winning 23.2% and 9.9% of the vote ​respectively. A fourth party, [[Prosperous Armenia]], narrowly missed entering parliament after a later tally of [[electronic vote|electronic votes]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/armenias-ruling-party-leads-parliamentary-vote-with-57-early-results-2026-06-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 Jersey general election]]
**Declared results indicate that [[Reform Jersey]] leader [[Sam Mézec]] will not be re-elected to the [[States Assembly]] after placing tenth in the senatorial race. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ce8jvd6ynnno (BBC News)]
*[[Illegal immigration to India]]
**The [[Government of West Bengal|government]] of [[West Bengal]], [[India]], deports nearly 5,000 [[Bangladesh]]i nationals and detains hundreds more as part of a campaign targeting [[undocumented migrants]] following [[2026 West Bengal Legislative Assembly election|the state's recent election]]. [https://tribune.net.ph/2026/06/08/5000-bangladeshis-booted (AFP via ''Daily Tribune'')]
*Former [[Supreme Court of Canada|Supreme Court]] justice and [[Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights|United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights]] [[Louise Arbour]] is sworn in as the 31st [[Governor General of Canada]]. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/article/louise-arbour-becomes-canadas-31st-governor-general/ (CTV)]
